sections.title: Species and habit
sections.text: The catalogue entry Coffea refers here to Coffea arabica, Arabica coffee, rather than the whole genus. In the wild it is an evergreen shrub or small tree about 2–8 m tall, native to humid forests of Ethiopia and neighbouring parts of eastern Africa. In cultivation it is often pruned shorter.

sections.title: Fruits and coffee
sections.text: The fruits are bright red drupes, sometimes yellow or purple, usually with two seeds. The pulp is eaten in some uses; dried, processed and roasted seeds are brewed as coffee and contain caffeine. The plate matches the branches, berries and cut seeds.
